title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Copilot Credits usage report for pay-as-you-go in Copilot Chat
summary: Pass: the report's scope, controls, default and licensing caveats are supported by Microsoft's documentation and notice. One rollout sentence should retain Microsoft's qualification that completion by the end of May 2027 is expected, rather than certain.

claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists no platforms.

claims.claim: Open the report in the Microsoft 365 admin center at Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot > Credits.
claims.quote: In the navigation menu, select Reports. If you don't see Reports, select Show all, and then select Reports. Select Usage. On the Usage page, under Reports, select Microsoft Copilot, and then select Credits.

claims.claim: The report shows total credits used for Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go billing policies.
claims.quote: This report gives you visibility into credits used for your Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go billing policies. It includes key metrics such as: Total credits used

claims.claim: The report includes cumulative and daily time series.
claims.quote: Cumulative and daily time series

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The report breaks down credits used per user.
claims.quote: Credits used per user, per agent, per billing policy, and per agent-user pair

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The report breaks down credits used per agent.
claims.quote: Credits used per user, per agent, per billing policy, and per agent-user pair

claims.claim: The report breaks down credits used per billing policy.
claims.quote: Credits used per user, per agent, per billing policy, and per agent-user pair

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The report breaks down credits used per agent-user pair.
claims.quote: Credits used per user, per agent, per billing policy, and per agent-user pair

claims.claim: Usage can be viewed within about an hour of interaction with a metered agent.
claims.quote: You can view usage within an hour from when users interact with a metered agent.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The report alerts administrators to users consuming more than 2,000 credits.
claims.quote: To help you mitigate overspending, the report includes alerts when users in your organization use more than 2,000 credits.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: During preview, the report displays at most 30 days of consumption history.
claims.quote: During preview, the report displays a maximum of 30 days of Copilot Credits history.

claims.claim: Usage before 3 May 2025 is unavailable in the report.
claims.quote: In addition, usage information from before May 3, 2025, isn't available in the report.

claims.claim: Microsoft updated notice MC1069563 on 28 October 2026.
claims.quote: Updated October 28, 2026: We have updated the timeline below.

claims.claim: The notice schedules the start of Worldwide GA rollout for the end of April 2027, previously early January.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in end of April 2027 (previously early January)

claims.claim: The notice's rollout window completes by the end of May 2027, previously the end of January.
claims.quote: and expect to complete by end of May 2027 (previously end of January).
claims.fix: Replace 'and completes by the end of May 2027 (previously end of January)' with 'and is expected to complete by the end of May 2027 (previously end of January)'.

claims.claim: The report rolls out automatically with no admin action required before rollout.
claims.quote: This rollout will happen automatically by the specified date with no admin action required before the rollout.

claims.claim: The report is on by default.
claims.quote: This new report will be on by default

claims.claim: The notice names Reporting > Usage > Microsoft 365 Copilot > Message consumption as the report path.
claims.quote: will be available in the Microsoft admin center at Reporting > Usage > Microsoft 365 Copilot > Message consumption:

claims.claim: The report appears after Copilot Chat pay-as-you-go is set up in either admin center and agent usage is enabled.
claims.quote: After you set up pay-as-you-go for Microsoft Copilot Chat, either in the Microsoft 365 admin center or the Power Platform admin center, and enable agent usage in your organization, you see a new report that includes metrics for credits used.

claims.claim: Copilot Chat consumption appears even when its billing policy was configured in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: You can set up the pay-as-you-go billing policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center or Power Platform admin center. If you configure pay-as-you-go, and users without a Microsoft Copilot license use metered agents in Copilot Chat, the data appears in the report.

claims.claim: The report covers users without a Microsoft Copilot license interacting with agents in Copilot Chat that use the Copilot Studio meter.
claims.quote: from interactions by users in your organization who don't have a Microsoft Copilot license and are interacting with agents in Copilot Chat that spin the Copilot Studio meter during the selected time period.

claims.claim: This is not a general report of all Copilot Studio agent consumption.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Copilot Credits report helps you manage metered consumption costs for Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Agent design influences the number of credits consumed.
claims.quote: The number of credits used depends on the design of the agent, how often users interact with it, and the features the agent uses.

claims.claim: The documented example combines 10 credits for tenant graph grounding and 2 for generative answers for a prompt.
claims.quote: For example, an agent grounded in a tenant graph could use 12 credits (10 credits for tenant graph-grounding, and two credits for generative answers) to respond to a single complex prompt from a user.

claims.claim: The report's alert user details can be viewed and exported to CSV.
claims.quote: Select View Copilot credits details to see the user list and export it to CSV.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Usernames, display names, groups and sites are hidden by default in usage reports.
claims.quote: By default, user-specific information like usernames, display names, groups, and sites is hidden in usage reports.

claims.claim: Usage Summary Reports Reader can view usage reports without user details.
claims.quote: Usage Summary Reports Reader (with no user details).

claims.claim: Global Administrator is among the roles permitted to view usage reports.
claims.quote: To view usage reports, you must have one of the following permissions: Global Administrator

claims.claim: Exchange Administrator is among the roles permitted to view usage reports.
claims.quote: Exchange Administrator

claims.claim: SharePoint Administrator is among the roles permitted to view usage reports.
claims.quote: SharePoint Administrator

claims.claim: Reports Reader is among the roles permitted to view usage reports.
claims.quote: Reports Reader

claims.claim: Teams Administrator is among the roles permitted to view usage reports.
claims.quote: Teams Administrator

claims.claim: AI Administrator is among the roles permitted to view usage reports.
claims.quote: AI Administrator

claims.claim: The Copilot reporting options page lists AI Administrator as a role that accesses Copilot reports.
claims.quote: AI Administrator: Accesses the Copilot reports.

claims.claim: The tenant-wide name concealment setting also affects the report's Billing Policy ID.
claims.quote: Changes to this hidden data setting affect the username, display name, and Billing Policy ID.

claims.claim: The tenant concealment setting is at Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: Select Org Settings. On the Services tab, select Reports. In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/admin/reportSettings with { "displayConcealedNames": true } updates the tenant reporting privacy setting.
displayConcealedNames true conceals user information across reports and false shows identifiable information.
claims.quote: If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.claim: The cited reportSettings API is beta and not supported for production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; What's changing; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The Consumption tab is at Copilot > Cost Management > Consumption in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. Select the Consumption tab.

claims.claim: The Consumption tab reports Copilot Credit usage by spending policy, user, group, agent and service.
claims.quote: The Consumption tab provides reporting experiences for copilot credit usage by: Spending policy User Group Agent Service

claims.claim: Cost Management covers supported services governed through Microsoft 365 usage-based billing policies.
claims.quote: Use Copilot > Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center when you want to manage and monitor Copilot Credit usage for services governed by Microsoft 365 usage-based billing policies.

claims.claim: Learn does not present the Cost Management Consumption tab as a replacement for the Copilot Chat Credits report.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Credits report" "Cost Management" "replace". Opened Microsoft Copilot Credits report, Monitor Copilot Credit spending, and the admin-center-versus-Azure-bill comparison; no replacement statement found.

claims.claim: The per-user consumption operation is GET /beta/copilot/costManagement/usageReports/userUsageRecords?startDate={startDate}&endDate={endDate}.
claims.quote:
GET /copilot/costManagement/usageReports/userUsageRecords?startDate={startDate}&endDate={endDate}
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/usageReports/userUsageRecords?startDate=2026-07-01&endDate=2026-07-02&$orderby=consumedQuantity desc&$top=2&$count=true

claims.claim: The userUsageRecords operation reports per-user consumption for exactly one completed UTC day per call.
claims.quote: The range must select exactly one completed UTC day. Current-day, future, and multi-day ranges are rejected, not clamped.

claims.claim: The userUsageRecords operation supports delegated work or school permissions only.
claims.quote:
Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotCostManagement-UserData.Read.All | CopilotCostManagement.Read.All
Delegated (personal Microsoft account) | Not supported. | Not supported.
Application | Not supported. | Not supported.

claims.claim: The Cost Management userUsageRecords API is beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The per-user Cost Management API call is not an equivalent for every Consumption tab breakdown or the dedicated Credits report.
claims.quote: Get a list of costManagementUserUsageRecord objects that report each user's consumption of Copilot Credits for one completed UTC day, ranked by consumption.

claims.claim: No API for the dedicated Credits report itself is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/graph "Copilot" "credits report" API; "Copilot Credits report" "export" "API" Graph PowerShell. Opened the Credits report and Cost Management API overview/reference; found no dedicated Credits-report endpoint.

claims.claim: No additional report-specific administrative configuration is documented beyond report access and name concealment.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Credits report" "configure" "settings" API. Opened the Credits report, usage reports overview, reportSettings update, and Cost Management API overview; no additional report-specific administrative setting found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft's notice says a Microsoft Copilot license is not required for this pay-as-you-go scenario.
claims.quote: This message refers to Microsoft Copilot in a pay-as-you-go model. A Microsoft Copilot license is not required.

claims.claim: A separate licensing or pricing model for the report itself is not published, so its licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Credits report" "settings" "license" price. Read the Credits report, usage reports overview, pay-as-you-go service overview and meters page, plus MC1069563; none publishes a separate report licence or report price.

claims.claim: The Credits report documentation states no separate price for the report.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Credits report" "settings" "license" price. Read Microsoft Copilot Credits report in full, including its prerequisites and FAQ; no separate report price is stated.

claims.claim: The consumption reported is metered in Copilot Credits through pay-as-you-go billing policies.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Copilot Credits report helps you manage metered consumption costs for Microsoft Copilot Chat. This report gives you visibility into credits used for your Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go billing policies.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go usage can take 24 hours to appear in Azure Cost Management.
claims.quote: To view costs in the Azure portal, see What is Microsoft Cost Management? ... Billed amounts are updated daily and sometimes more frequently. It can take 24 hours after usage of a service to show in Microsoft Cost Management.

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management is billing-oriented and lacks the same user-level and spending-policy context as the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Shows billing-oriented cost data, such as costs by subscription, service, resource, meter, or invoice period. It doesn't show the same user-level or spending-policy context as the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The usage reports overview lists Copilot reports as unavailable in some government clouds.
claims.quote:
| Report | Public | GCC | GCC-High | DoD | Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet |
| Microsoft Copilot credits | Yes | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A |
